title: Rav Shishah

paragraphs: In Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 19:1, Rabbi Shmuel [bar] Avduma needed to circumcise his son Shishah but forgot the knife. He consulted Rabbi Mana, then Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elazar. The Rif there reads Shishna.

notes.text: The consulted Shabbat paragraph has Shmuel bar Avduma and explicitly identifies Shishah as his son, with the title Rav. The supplied גר and אצל wording is garbled; the bracketed bar and corrected relationship remain proposed local English, with the source question open. Shishna is the Rif variant Hyman reports.

The saved whole Guggenheimer Shabbat19:1 scalar explicitly has Rabbi Shmuel bar Avduma circumcising Rav Shishah his son, then consulting Rabbi Mana and Rabbi Yitzchak bar Elazar. This supports the bracketed bar and son relationship despite supplied גר and אצל, but does not prove how the printed glyphs arose. Hyman’s ben Elazar remains beside the named bar form; the vocalization of ששעה remains uncertain. Shishna is the Rif variant Hyman reports, not a newly inspected Rif witness or identity binding.

Hyman’s printed Hebrew has ger Avdomi and uses etzel. Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 19:1 gives Shmuel bar Avduma and calls Rav Shishah his son. It names Yitzchak bar Elazar as the second rabbi consulted. In the Vilna Rif (Shabbat 52a–52b), Shmuel is bar Avdimi, his son is Rav Shishna, and the second rabbi is Yitzchak beRabbi Elazar. In both versions, the people involved forgot to bring the knife, and the circumcision is postponed until the next day.
